claims.quote: Common options for most adults who have not received ART before include INSTI-based combinations such as bictegravir/ tenofovir alafenamide / emtricitabine

claims.text: Coformulated bictegravir is contraindicated with rifampin or rifabutin TB treatment (they lower its levels and risk ART failure).
claims.quote: coformulated bictegravir is contraindicated when co-administered with a tuberculosis treatment containing rifampin or rifabutin. Rifampin and rifabutin strongly induce the metabolism of bictegravir, reducing its levels and predisposing the patient to ART failure.

claims.text: Long-acting cabotegravir (INSTI) + rilpivirine (NNRTI): IM injection every 2 months,
claims.quote: rilpivirine, a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI), and cabotegravir, an integrase inhibitor. The regimen can be administered as an intramuscular injection every 2 months.

claims.text: for adults on a stable regimen who are virologically suppressed.
claims.quote: must be adults who are on an otherwise stable regimen and who are virologically suppressed

claims.text: Often started orally for 4 weeks to check tolerance.
claims.quote: Patients often start their treatment with oral cabotegravir and rilpivirine for 4 weeks to assess how well they tolerate the medications.

claims.text: Patients with active hepatitis B are often excluded (no hepatitis B activity).
claims.quote: Patients with active hepatitis B infection are often excluded, because this regimen does not have treatment spectrum against hepatitis B.

claims.text: Lenacapavir (capsid inhibitor): injection every 6 months with an optimized background regimen, for heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug resistance.
claims.quote: capsid inhibitor that is used in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug resistance. It is typically administered as an intramuscular injection every 6 months as part of an optimized background antiretroviral regimen
